themes.theme: History and Rationale for Reviewing the Regulations
themes.reason: Provides background on when regulations were last updated and that a review was triggered, but this is procedural context rather than the substantive diagnosis of why outdated testing drives chemical use.

themes.theme: Safety Benefits and Protective Effectiveness of Current Regulations
themes.reason: Establishes that current regulations do work to prevent harm, which frames the tension the diagnosis must address (safety vs chemical harm) and is a necessary counterweight to justify why change is needed rather than wholesale repeal.

themes.theme: Health and Environmental Harms of Flame Retardant Chemicals
themes.reason: This is the core evidence of the 'chemical use' harm half of the problem statement—without this theme there is no case that chemical use from flammability testing causes harm.

themes.theme: Flaws in the Testing Regime and Compliance Methods
themes.reason: This directly explains the causal mechanism—how outdated match testing forces manufacturers to over-use flame retardants—making it the central diagnosis of why the regulation drives chemical use.

themes.theme: Scope, Definitions and Traceability of Regulatory Framework
themes.reason: Addresses separate administrative gaps (scope ambiguity, traceability) not directly tied to the causal link between testing and chemical use; a secondary, non-essential point.
